finding: UNOSAT data of 2 September 2026: about 65 km² of the roughly 1,246 km² it examined appears to be affected by the flood.

measurement.source: UNOSAT geodatabase FL20260826NPL (layers AnalysisExtent and FloodExtent)

check.method: geodesic area on WGS84 (pyproj Geod) of the same polygons; 100 % of the affected area lies inside the analysed area

measurement.scope: UNOSAT's whole analysis area (Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts). The app draws the full layer, simplified by about 5 m (not clipped); the image frame shows only a small part of it (about 2.3 km² of the affected area).
measurement.status: Preliminary assessment: UNOSAT says it has not been validated in the field.

history.what: UNOSAT map 4259 printed about 37 km² affected within about 350 km² analysed, for the analysis as of 28 August 2026.

sources.publisher: UNOSAT lake data on HDX (CC BY-SA)
EU Space: Aftermath of Nepal flash flood
ESA: Sentinel-2 captures before and after Nepal flash flood
ESA: Nepal glacier collapse and flood – before and after
Reuters: Nepal lake breaks banks (28 August 2026)
ICIMOD: Understanding the Gyirong–Rasuwa disaster of 26 August 2026

score._doc: Evidence score: how well the evidence supports the finding, 25 points per criterion (levels 25 / 15 / 5 / 0). points null = assessment incomplete. Not a map accuracy percentage.

criteria.name: Coverage
criteria.rule: 25: the analysed area contains at least 95 % of the image frame and the whole collapse area; 15: at least 75 %; 5: at least 25 %; 0: less.
criteria.reason: UNOSAT's analysed area contains the whole collapse area and the two lakes, but only 88 % of the Betrawati–Gerkhu frame (measured here); all of the affected area in the frame lies inside it.

criteria.name: Timing of the images
criteria.rule: 25: imagery from the day of the event or the day after; 15: within 7 days; 5: within 30 days; 0: later, or before the event.
criteria.reason: UNOSAT used PlanetScope images of 26 August (the day of the flood) and Sentinel-2 of 27 August.

criteria.name: Comparability
criteria.rule: 25: same sensor and date as the app's image, method documented; 15: same date but other sensors added or the method only briefly described; 5: other dates or sensors only; 0: cannot be compared.
criteria.reason: Same Sentinel-2 date (27 August) as the app's after image, but UNOSAT also used PlanetScope and describes its method only briefly.

criteria.name: Independent support
criteria.rule: 25: an independent map of the same area was compared here and agrees; 15: independent maps of the same area exist but were not compared here; 5: only reports or photos; 0: none.
criteria.reason: ICIMOD mapped the flood extent along the same valley (Landsat, Sentinel-2, PlanetScope) and Copernicus EMS mapped it under activation EMSR927; neither was compared with UNOSAT's outline here.
